title: Open-restriction compatibility of local Ext and internal-Hom hypercohomology
statement:
Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], using its site of opens with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in a common universe containing its opens and module values [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $K,L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be arbitrary objects of the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Put $A=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(K,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For any open $U$, $K_U,L_U$ denote termwise derived restrictions to its restricted structure sheaf. Write $H^i(U,A)=H^i(R\Gamma(U,A))$, where $R\Gamma(U,-)$ is unbounded derived evaluation at $U$, computed on K-injective representatives and followed by forgetting scalars [def-sfb-right-derived-functor, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For every integer $i$ there are canonical additive isomorphisms
$$\alpha_U^i:H^i(U,A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(K_U,L_U[i])$$
which form an isomorphism of abelian presheaves on $X$: for each inclusion $j:W\subseteq U$ and every $a\in H^i(U,A)$,
$$\alpha_W^i(\operatorname{res}_{U,W}a)=\operatorname{res}^{D}_{U,W}(\alpha_U^i(a)).$$
Here the left restriction is induced by evaluation of a representative complex on smaller opens; the right restriction is exact derived open restriction with its canonical composition and shift isomorphisms [def-trf-ringed-derived-open-hom-restriction], applied to the pair $K,L[i]$. The comparisons are natural contravariantly in $K$ and covariantly in $L$, and compatible with successive open restrictions. No boundedness or local-freeness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08DK (cohomology-lemma-section-RHom-over-U), all shifts and open-restriction naturality

proof.text: Choose complexes E,M representing K,L. On the small site of opens, choose a functorial K-injective resolution M→I, and a K-flat resolution t:P→E, using the two existence statements cited below. Set C=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I) and B=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I). The definition of derived internal Hom identifies QC with A, where Q is derived localization. The induced map b:C→B is a quasi-isomorphism by the well-definedness lemma, applied with s=id_I and t. The K-flat/K-injective Hom lemma makes B K-injective. Crucially, the section quasi-isomorphism lemma also says Γ(U,b) is a quasi-isomorphism for every open U; a quasi-isomorphism of sheaf complexes alone would not justify this last assertion. All these results allow unbounded complexes and apply to the commutative structure sheaf in the stipulated universe.

source.place: Tag 08DK, cohomology-lemma-section-RHom-over-U, choice of resolutions; cohomology-lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective and cohomology-lemma-RHom-well-defined

proof.text: Let η_{U,C}:QΓ(U,C)→RΓ(U,QC) be the derived-evaluation unit. Its naturality for b gives a commutative square with top arrow QΓ(U,b), bottom arrow RΓ(U,Qb), and right arrow η_{U,B}. The top and bottom arrows are isomorphisms by Step 1, and η_{U,B} is an isomorphism since B is K-injective. Thus η_{U,C} is an isomorphism for every U. This uses the unit characterization of the right derived functor, not an assumption that C itself is K-injective. Concretely, take a single functorial K-injective resolution c:C→J on X. The unit is represented for every U by Γ(U,c):Γ(U,C)→Γ(U,J), and all restriction maps on RΓ(U,QC) are represented by restrictions of Γ(U,J). Hence these units commute with open restrictions: res_{U,W}Γ(U,c)=Γ(W,c)res_{U,W}.

source.place: Tag 08DK, cohomology-lemma-section-RHom-over-U, computation by sections; cohomology.tex section-unbounded, derived evaluation on K-injectives

proof.text: For each U and integer i, apply the canonical sections comparison to E,I. It gives H^iΓ(U,C)≅Hom_{K(\mathcal O_U)}(E_U,I_U[i]), specified on a cocycle z by the homotopy class of the shifted chain map f_z whose components are the evaluated Hom-complex projections. Restriction of I to U is K-injective by the localized-restriction lemma. Its shift I_U[i] is K-injective as well: a map from an acyclic N into I_U[i] corresponds to a map from the acyclic N[-i] into I_U, so is null homotopic. The K-injective localization lemma therefore identifies this homotopy Hom group with Hom_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(K_U,L_U[i]). Denote the resulting map by β_U^i; its representative formula is [z]↦Q_U(f_z), with the identifications QE_U=K_U and QI_U=L_U and the canonical shift comparison understood. It is additive: the projection formula sends z+z′ to f_z+f_{z′}, and homotopy quotient and derived localization preserve sums. Define α_U^i=β_U^i∘H^i(η_{U,C})^{-1}. Both factors are isomorphisms, so this gives the asserted additive isomorphism in every integer degree.

For j:W⊆U and a degree-i cocycle z over U, the projection defining its p-th component is a map of sheaves. Its value after restriction is therefore (z^p)|_W. Consequently the shifted chain map associated with res(z) is the restriction of f_z: the signs in the shift depend only on i and the cochain degree, and restriction preserves them. The same assertion for a degree-(i−1) cochain h shows res(dh)=d(res h), so it holds on cohomology classes. In the notation of the derived-open-restriction definition, naturality of the comparison e:R_U S_j≅R_W gives
\[e_E^{-1};S_j(Q_U(f_z));e_{I[i]}=Q_W(f_{\operatorname{res}z}).\]
Here the source and target use the canonical restriction/shift identifications; this is precisely the definition's conjugation formula for res^D, not an identification of unrelated Hom groups. Thus β_W^i(res[z])=res^D(β_U^i[z]). Step 2 gives the same commuting square for η. Since its components are invertible, composing these two squares proves α_W^i(res a)=res^D(α_U^i(a)) for every a.

source.place: cohomology-equation-cohomology-hom-complex and Tag 08DL, cohomology-lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U; componentwise elaboration of open-restriction naturality

proof.text: For chain maps t:E′→E and s:I→I′, the map on Hom-complex cochains is z↦szt; the associated shifted chain map is s[i]∘f_z∘t. The canonical comparison and the derived-naturality lemma therefore make β contravariantly natural in E and covariantly natural in I. With the functorial resolutions fixed in Steps 1–2, both c:C→J and the induced unit maps are natural as well. Thus α is natural on pairs of representing complexes. If either representing map is a quasi-isomorphism, the well-definedness and section quasi-isomorphism lemmas invert it, and the derived restriction functors invert it by their definition. The universal property of localization consequently descends these commuting squares to arbitrary morphisms in D(\mathcal O_X), contravariantly in K and covariantly in L. The same naturality, applied to the resolution maps M→I and to the comparison with any other resolution, shows that the comparisons so obtained agree under the canonical identifications of representatives: both send a cocycle to its localized chain map. Hence the maps are canonical, rather than dependent on E,M,I or J.

source.place: cohomology-equation-cohomology-hom-complex, cohomology-lemma-RHom-well-defined, and construction in cohomology-section-internal-hom; naturality of the displayed maps

proof.text: For V⊆W⊆U, restricting each component of a cochain twice gives its restriction directly from U to V. The same holds for c:C→J. Therefore the two commuting squares of Step 4 compose to the square for V⊆U; for U⊆U they are identity squares. On the derived-Hom side the comparison maps e are induced by these same composition identifications of restriction functors, so the middle e and e^{-1} cancel in the two successive conjugations. This proves compatibility with successive restrictions. Each β is additive and each η is an additive isomorphism, so the α_U^i assemble to an isomorphism of abelian presheaves. No step imposed boundedness or local freeness.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q18-3273053dc (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 6 steps and the 15 cited statements in full against Stacks cohomology.tex 08DK (l.10581, lemma-section-RHom-over-U) and 08DL (l.10640). The delivery adds no new nodes. The statement is byte-identical to live, which is still unsplit. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and nothing cites SGA. Step 1 builds C=Hom(E,I) and B=Hom(P,I) with P K-flat. It applies rhom-well-defined with s=id_I and t:P→E, hom-kflat-into-kinjective (B is K-injective) and hom-complex-sections-quasi-iso (Γ(U,b) is a quasi-iso for every U). Step 2 uses the naturality square of the unit η (def-sfb-right-derived-functor) to show η_C is an isomorphism even though C need not be K-injective. Step 3 uses the canonical-comparison formula, K-injectivity of I|_U and of its shift (also for negative i), and kinjective-hom-derived; this gives an additive isomorphism α in every degree. Step 4 is an elementary restriction square. The p-th projection is a sheaf map, and the e-conjugation formula of def-trf-ringed-derived-open-hom-restriction applies; Lean `res` = overFunctor in both nodes. Step 5 gets naturality from (szt)^p=s z^p t, then descends through the localization Ch^op×Ch→D^op×D. Step 6: successive restrictions compose and e/e^{-1} cancel. Edge cases: U=∅, zero K or L, W=U, and a one-point space, which gives H^i RHom_R(K,L)=Hom_D(K,L[i]). The duplicate search found only degree-0 special tools (pur-rhom-into-kinjective-local, pur-localized-hom-complex-homotopy) and tensor/evaluation slice comparisons. I accept the eight tool_uses as generic ringed-site homological algebra. The blueprint ancestry is inherited and unchanged. No fixes.
